pathway.title: Wayfair Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage has fallen because earnings recovered, since net debt barely moved: it was USD 1,802 million at FY2024, USD 1,796 million at FY2025 and USD 1,761 million at 2026-09-30, because lower gross debt was paid largely from cash (pro forma for the USD 64 million settlement of 2026-10-28: not established). Net debt over issuer-adjusted EBITDA went from 3.98x in FY2024 to 2.42x in FY2025 and 2.06x over the last twelve months, while the same ratio on reported EBITDA is 5.58x and 3.21x, and add-backs are 35.64% of last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA. Creditors should treat the reported-basis ratios as the test of cash earning power and the adjusted ratios as the view closer to a covenant definition. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7

- Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months and is the main support. Cash of USD 1,038 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 418 million give USD 1,456 million, 2.31x the USD 631 million of visible needs (the 2027 convertible notes, a year of cash interest and a year of capital expenditure), and no other principal falls due before 2029. The USD 418 million is already net of USD 82 million of letters of credit, but drawing it depends on covenant compliance that cannot be tested, and payables of USD 1,213 million exceed cash, so the cash is not surplus (pro forma for the USD 64 million settlement of 2026-10-28: not established). Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_w-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

- The business model funds itself from customers and suppliers, so the main route to stress is an order decline that reverses that float. About 97.8% of nine-month 2026 revenue was collected before recognition and payables were 13.63x inventories, and USD 140 million of the USD 174 million rise in operating cash flow came from working capital, equal to 9.62% of liquidity. A volume fall would turn that inflow into an outflow quickly, before reported earnings fall. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C4

- Debt service is covered but with limited margin on reported earnings. Cash interest paid rose by USD 107 million from FY2024 to the last twelve months as secured notes replaced convertible notes, and reported EBITDA covers it 3.23x against 5.02x for adjusted EBITDA, with senior secured debt at 4.68x reported EBITDA. If reported EBITDA fell back to the FY2025 level of USD 322 million, cover on the last-twelve-month cash interest would be 1.89x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C8; calculation C5; calculation C9

- Refinancing capacity looks adequate: the maturity wall is laddered and market access was shown four times. Principal of USD 229 million falls due in 2027, USD 800 million in 2029, USD 700 million each in 2030 and 2032 and USD 400 million in 2034, and Wayfair LLC issued four secured series since 2024. The cost is a larger secured block that sits ahead of unsecured claims, so unsecured claims, including the 2027 convertible notes, rank behind it. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_w-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130

- Financial policy is the main judgement call: founders control the votes and the repurchase room is as large as the cash balance. The co-founders and affiliates held 67.4% of voting power, no dividend has ever been paid and total debt fell USD 473 million in 2026, but USD 1,028 million of repurchase authority equals 99.04% of cash and the indentures that would limit it are not supplied. Creditors therefore depend on the observed debt-reduction record rather than on documented limits. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C10

- Profit is concentrated in the U.S. and the group has no diversification in category. The U.S. earned a 7.78% segment Adjusted EBITDA margin on 88.93% of nine-month 2026 revenue while International lost USD 54 million, and the category is largely unbranded and highly substitutable, so competition shows up in order value, which fell 1.89% in Q3 2026 even as orders rose 12.2%. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_w-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_w-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30

runs.text: The first strength is liquidity against near-term needs: cash of USD 1,038 million and USD 418 million of undrawn revolver cover the 2027 convertible notes, a year of cash interest and capital spending 2.31x, so a short disruption would not force refinancing before 2029 (pro forma for the USD 64 million settlement of 2026-10-28: not established). The second is earnings recovery with improving leverage: adjusted EBITDA of USD 853 million over the last twelve months and net debt over adjusted EBITDA of 2.06x against 3.98x in FY2024 show deleveraging that was led by earnings and by USD 473 million of lower debt. The third is a laddered maturity profile and demonstrated market access, with USD 2,572 million of secured notes due 2029 to 2034 replacing earlier convertible debt and USD 229 million due in 2027, which lowers refinancing risk through 2028. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3

The first weakness is dependence on a working-capital float: payables are 13.63x inventories and USD 140 million of the rise in operating cash flow was working capital, so an order decline would hit cash before earnings. The second is thin reported earnings and heavy reliance on add-backs: reported EBITDA of USD 549 million is below the USD 853 million adjusted figure by 35.64%, and net leverage on reported EBITDA is 3.21x. The third is financial-policy and priority risk: founders hold 67.4% of the votes, USD 1,028 million of repurchase authority remains, and the secured notes of USD 2,572 million rank ahead of the 2027 convertible notes while the debt documents are not supplied. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No acquisition, merger or sponsor transaction is described in the supplied documents, so the transaction record is the issuer's own financing and portfolio actions. Wayfair LLC issued USD 800 million of secured notes due 2029 on 2024-10-08, USD 700 million due 2030 on 2025-03-13, USD 700 million due 2032 on 2025-11-07 and USD 400 million due 2034 on 2026-05-18. The 2030 issue funded the repurchase of USD 578 million of 2026 convertible notes on 2025-03-14, and the 2034 issue, with cash, funded the settlement of the 2028 convertible notes, so secured debt has replaced unsecured convertible debt step by step. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_w-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-K_2025-12-31_w-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_w-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_w-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-06-30_w-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12

The 2026 actions were the redemption of USD 250 million of 2027 convertible notes on 2026-03-23, the redemption of the remaining USD 444 million of 2028 convertible notes on 2026-06-29 with the 2034 proceeds and cash, the maturity payment of USD 39 million on the 2026 convertible notes on 2026-08-15, and the USD 60 million of share repurchases in Q3 2026 together with an equity instrument, bought for USD 60 million, that settled on 2026-10-28 for a USD 64 million cash settlement. These actions lowered total debt by USD 473 million between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30 but left the secured series at USD 2,572 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_w-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_w-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C17; calculation C18

fields.value: Wayfair's leverage has fallen but depends on adjusted earnings: net debt of USD 1,761 million at 2026-09-30 is 2.06x issuer-adjusted EBITDA but 3.21x reported EBITDA, so creditors rely on USD 304 million of last-twelve-month add-backs. fields.value: Wayfair Inc. (issuer id w), as of 2026-11-05, credit_snapshot pathway (the full credit assessment). Scope: the issuer's business, ownership and control, operating model, governance and capital-allocation behaviour and its dated history, from the supplied annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wayfair is founder-controlled with no sponsor, so creditor risk lies in concentrated voting control and in how cash is split between buybacks and debt reduction, not in a sponsor's extraction record. The co-founders and their affiliates held 67.4% of the votes but 18.3% of the economic interest at 2025-12-31, the supplied documents describe no dividend and no creditor-adverse transaction, and total debt fell by USD 473 million to 2026-09-30 while USD 60 million went to buybacks in Q3 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a drop-ship retailer whose customers pay before delivery, so supplier payables of USD 1,213 million fund inventory of USD 89 million and a fall in order volume would drain cash first. Profit comes from the U.S.: segment Adjusted EBITDA was USD 683 million in the nine months of 2026, against a USD 54 million loss in International.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control sits with the co-founders, not with a sponsor or the public holders. Class B shares carry ten votes each, so the co-founders and their affiliates, with 18.3% of the economic interest, held 67.4% of the voting power at 2025-12-31 and can approve a merger, a sale of assets or a charter amendment without the other holders. The control is wearing down slowly: Class B was 15.33% of all shares at 2026-10-28 against 16.86% at 2025-12-31, and the charter ends the Class B structure when it falls below 10%, so creditors should expect the same people to direct strategy and capital returns for the foreseeable future.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital allocation so far favours debt reduction with a modest buyback, but the buyback room is large against cash. Total debt carrying value fell USD 473 million to USD 2,799 million, while Wayfair bought back USD 60 million of shares in Q3 2026 and paid USD 60 million for an equity instrument to facilitate repurchases, leaving USD 1,028 million authorised against cash of USD 1,038 million. The company has never paid a dividend, so a repurchase pace that outran cash generation, not a distribution, is the way value could leave creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The refinancing has moved debt up the capital structure. Wayfair LLC issued secured notes of USD 800 million due 2029, USD 700 million due 2030, USD 700 million due 2032 and USD 400 million due 2034 while unsecured convertible notes were repurchased or redeemed, so the secured series carried USD 2,572 million at 2026-09-30; the first three share first-priority liens with the revolver, the 2034 notes are described as senior secured, and the remaining USD 227 million of 2027 convertible notes are effectively subordinated to them. This extends maturities and cuts the convertible share overhang, at the price of more encumbered assets for any creditor outside the secured group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The operating model funds itself from customers and suppliers, which makes liquidity sensitive to volume. About 97.8% of net revenue in the nine months of 2026 was collected before it was recognised, payables were 13.63x inventories, and contract liabilities rose USD 19 million to USD 296 million, so a drop in orders could reverse payables and customer advances before it reduced reported earnings. Operating cash flow already carries this effect: the net change in operating assets and liabilities was an inflow of USD 64 million in the nine months of 2026 against an outflow of USD 76 million a year earlier.

A creditor therefore underwrites U.S. execution, with International a drag that management has reshaped by leaving Germany.

fields.value: - Disclosure supports monitoring, but governance detail is not established. Each quarterly report is signed the same day as its earnings release, the auditor changed to a new firm for 2025 and reported internal control as effective, yet board composition, related-party dealings and executive pay sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so related-party leakage and board independence cannot be assessed either way. Missing evidence is not read as adverse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Trade, duty and platform dependencies are real but not quantified. Management calls the trade environment fluid and highly uncertain, Wayfair relies solely on one cloud provider for parts of its operations, and Canadian customs reviews cost about USD 14 million and USD 19 million of duties paid in 2025 against a USD 45 million benefit recorded, so the exposure is a margin risk to monitor rather than a measured loss.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a benign reading is that the same holders who control 67.4% of the votes have an authorisation of USD 1,028 million to repurchase shares, almost the whole of the USD 1,038 million cash balance, and that the indentures and the credit agreement are not supplied, so nothing in the documents limits how much of that room could be used. The company has so far repurchased USD 60 million of shares in 2026, paid USD 60 million for an equity instrument and reduced debt by USD 473 million, which supports the view that debt reduction comes first. The view would weaken if a proxy statement showed related-party payments to controlling holders, if repurchases were funded by drawing the revolver or by new secured debt, if the 2027 convertible notes drew a large cash conversion call while cash was falling, or if the working-capital inflow reversed as orders slowed. It would improve if the next quarterly reports show buybacks held at the current pace with cash steady and International losses narrowing.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_w-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage has fallen because earnings recovered, since net debt barely moved: it was USD 1,802 million at FY2024, USD 1,796 million at FY2025 and USD 1,761 million at 2026-09-30, because lower gross debt was paid largely from cash (pro forma for the USD 64 million settlement of 2026-10-28: not established). Net debt over issuer-adjusted EBITDA went from 3.98x in FY2024 to 2.42x in FY2025 and 2.06x over the last twelve months, while the same ratio on reported EBITDA is 5.58x and 3.21x, and add-backs are 35.64% of last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA. Creditors should treat the reported-basis ratios as the test of cash earning power and the adjusted ratios as the view closer to a covenant definition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months and is the main support. Cash of USD 1,038 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 418 million give USD 1,456 million, 2.31x the USD 631 million of visible needs (the 2027 convertible notes, a year of cash interest and a year of capital expenditure), and no other principal falls due before 2029. The USD 418 million is already net of USD 82 million of letters of credit, but drawing it depends on covenant compliance that cannot be tested, and payables of USD 1,213 million exceed cash, so the cash is not surplus (pro forma for the USD 64 million settlement of 2026-10-28: not established).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_w-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business model funds itself from customers and suppliers, so the main route to stress is an order decline that reverses that float. About 97.8% of nine-month 2026 revenue was collected before recognition and payables were 13.63x inventories, and USD 140 million of the USD 174 million rise in operating cash flow came from working capital, equal to 9.62% of liquidity. A volume fall would turn that inflow into an outflow quickly, before reported earnings fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt service is covered but with limited margin on reported earnings. Cash interest paid rose by USD 107 million from FY2024 to the last twelve months as secured notes replaced convertible notes, and reported EBITDA covers it 3.23x against 5.02x for adjusted EBITDA, with senior secured debt at 4.68x reported EBITDA. If reported EBITDA fell back to the FY2025 level of USD 322 million, cover on the last-twelve-month cash interest would be 1.89x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C8; calculation C5; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing capacity looks adequate: the maturity wall is laddered and market access was shown four times. Principal of USD 229 million falls due in 2027, USD 800 million in 2029, USD 700 million each in 2030 and 2032 and USD 400 million in 2034, and Wayfair LLC issued four secured series since 2024. The cost is a larger secured block that sits ahead of unsecured claims, so unsecured claims, including the 2027 convertible notes, rank behind it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_w-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy is the main judgement call: founders control the votes and the repurchase room is as large as the cash balance. The co-founders and affiliates held 67.4% of voting power, no dividend has ever been paid and total debt fell USD 473 million in 2026, but USD 1,028 million of repurchase authority equals 99.04% of cash and the indentures that would limit it are not supplied. Creditors therefore depend on the observed debt-reduction record rather than on documented limits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Profit is concentrated in the U.S. and the group has no diversification in category. The U.S. earned a 7.78% segment Adjusted EBITDA margin on 88.93% of nine-month 2026 revenue while International lost USD 54 million, and the category is largely unbranded and highly substitutable, so competition shows up in order value, which fell 1.89% in Q3 2026 even as orders rose 12.2%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against the adequate view is that reported earnings are still thin: reported EBITDA was negative in FY2024 and USD 549 million over the last twelve months, the senior secured test of 4.0x in the revolver cannot be tested because its definition is not supplied, and senior secured debt is 4.68x reported EBITDA, which implies that the covenant definition adds back far more than reported EBITDA does. On the other side, adjusted EBITDA has risen from USD 453 million in FY2024 to USD 853 million over the last twelve months, cash interest is covered, debt has fallen and the maturities are laddered. The view would weaken if orders turned down while payables and customer advances unwound, if repurchases were funded from the revolver or new secured debt, if the 2027 convertible notes drew a large cash conversion call, or if International losses kept widening. It would strengthen with a second year of free cash flow near the last-twelve-month level without a working-capital inflow, and with a proxy statement and debt documents that show real limits on distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_w-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed indentures and the credit agreement are not supplied, so the senior secured leverage test, restricted-payment room and lien capacity cannot be examined, and the view of financial policy rests on the observed debt-reduction record alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No quantified management outlook is supplied, so the twelve-month cash needs used here are visible commitments and last-twelve-month actuals, not a forecast, and the downside path is qualitative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Business & governance records no liability management as described, while the annual report says Wayfair may use exchanges for equity or debt on its convertible notes; this is a stated possibility, not an executed action, and it is a watch item for the priority of the 2027 convertible notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The pro forma effect of the USD 64 million settlement on 2026-10-28 on net debt and leverage is not established because its direction is not stated, so every net debt figure here is at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is liquidity against near-term needs: cash of USD 1,038 million and USD 418 million of undrawn revolver cover the 2027 convertible notes, a year of cash interest and capital spending 2.31x, so a short disruption would not force refinancing before 2029 (pro forma for the USD 64 million settlement of 2026-10-28: not established). The second is earnings recovery with improving leverage: adjusted EBITDA of USD 853 million over the last twelve months and net debt over adjusted EBITDA of 2.06x against 3.98x in FY2024 show deleveraging that was led by earnings and by USD 473 million of lower debt. The third is a laddered maturity profile and demonstrated market access, with USD 2,572 million of secured notes due 2029 to 2034 replacing earlier convertible debt and USD 229 million due in 2027, which lowers refinancing risk through 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is dependence on a working-capital float: payables are 13.63x inventories and USD 140 million of the rise in operating cash flow was working capital, so an order decline would hit cash before earnings. The second is thin reported earnings and heavy reliance on add-backs: reported EBITDA of USD 549 million is below the USD 853 million adjusted figure by 35.64%, and net leverage on reported EBITDA is 3.21x. The third is financial-policy and priority risk: founders hold 67.4% of the votes, USD 1,028 million of repurchase authority remains, and the secured notes of USD 2,572 million rank ahead of the 2027 convertible notes while the debt documents are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wayfair is an online home-goods retailer whose customers pay at order and whose suppliers ship most orders directly, so the model supports cash-flow visibility through customer advances and low inventory but gives little contractual revenue visibility. Net revenue growth of 9.7% in Q3 2026 came from 12.2% more orders, with U.S. 88.93% of nine-month revenue and International losing USD 54 million, which means debt service capacity rests on U.S. order volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is founder-controlled and sponsor-free: the co-founders and affiliates held 67.4% of voting power against 18.3% of economic interest, Wayfair LLC issues the secured notes and borrows under the revolver, and Wayfair Inc. issues the convertible notes with guarantees from subsidiaries that are not named. This structure leaves capital returns to the founders' discretion, and the structural position of the unsecured convertible notes is behind the secured notes and the subsidiaries' liabilities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is volume-driven and discretionary: orders rose 12.2% while average order value fell 1.89% in Q3 2026, the repeat share of orders stayed near 80%, and the category is largely unbranded and highly substitutable. Pricing power is therefore weak, so revenue durability depends on traffic, supplier selection and promotions, and a downturn would show first in orders and then in thinner gross margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are largely variable: cost of goods sold was 70.4% of revenue in Q3 2026 and advertising 9.9%, while selling, operations, technology, general and administrative was 12.9%, so margins can be defended in a mild slowdown by cutting advertising but not in a sharp one because logistics and lease commitments are fixed, with operating lease liabilities of USD 1,025 million at 2025-12-31. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 2.5% in FY2023 to 6.0% in FY2025, which shows operating leverage works in both directions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_w-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low at 1.65% of FY2025 revenue and capital expenditure was USD 232 million over the last twelve months, so EBITDA converts to free cash flow of USD 476 million, 0.56 of adjusted EBITDA, but that conversion includes the working-capital inflow. Cash interest of USD 170 million and the recurring tax payments on equity awards are the leakage, which means free cash flow available for deleveraging is smaller than the headline figure when the float stops growing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense because the market is fragmented and includes furniture stores, big box retailers and online marketplaces, buyers can switch at low cost in an unbranded category, and the supplier base is wide, with about 20 thousand mostly small suppliers, so supplier power is low and the working-capital float is supplier-funded. New entrants and substitutes are not evidenced in the supplied documents beyond the named competitors, so they are not assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trade policy and duties matter because product cost is most of revenue: management calls the trade environment fluid and highly uncertain, and Canadian customs reviews cost about USD 14 million in 2025 against a USD 45 million benefit, so exposure is real but not quantified. Interest rates matter less for the issuer's drawn debt, which is fixed rate, but consumer demand for big-ticket home goods follows consumer spending, which is the sector headwind to monitor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scale and market position is average: last-twelve-month revenue of USD 13,207 million and 22.2 million active customers are large, but market share is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Competitive advantage is average: the logistics network and technology platform differentiate the offer, but the category is substitutable and order value is falling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Business diversification is weak: one category, 88.93% of revenue in the U.S. and a single cloud provider.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital intensity is low and advertising is flexible, while leases and logistics are fixed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin stability is weak: reported EBITDA was negative until FY2025 and adjusted margins of 2.5%, 3.8% and 6.0% show a recent recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow stability is average: USD 83 million, USD 329 million and USD 476 million over three periods is improving but includes a working-capital inflow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ability to refinance is average: four secured series were issued since 2024 and maturities are laddered, with no rating or market price supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity position is strong: USD 1,456 million against USD 631 million of visible needs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy and governance is average: no dividend and lower debt, offset by founder control and a large repurchase authority with documents not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No quantified outlook is supplied. Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the tailwinds are total order growth of 12.2% and U.S. revenue growth of 11.4% against a roughly flat U.S. category per management, operating leverage and lower debt, and the headwinds are tariffs and duties, falling order value, widening International losses and a possible cash call on the 2027 convertible notes, which are convertible in the quarter ending 2026-12-31 with an if-converted value USD 141 million above principal at 2026-09-30. Over three to five years the 2029 and 2030 maturities of USD 800 million and USD 700 million and the revolver maturity in 2030 define the refinancing window.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_a2026-11x04ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_w-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_w-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit-specific downside starts with a drop in order volume, for example from weaker consumer spending on big-ticket home goods or higher duties passed into prices. The first operating break is the working-capital float: payables of USD 1,213 million shrink with purchases and customer advances unwind, and the observed swing of USD 140 million between nine-month periods, equal to 9.62% of liquidity, shows the order of magnitude. Gross profit then falls on lower volume and promotions while cash interest of USD 170 million and lease and logistics commitments stay fixed, cash falls from USD 1,038 million (pro forma for the USD 64 million settlement of 2026-10-28: not established) and the revolver of USD 418 million is the second line of defence, with the 2027 convertible notes of USD 229 million the first principal due. Management levers are advertising, capital expenditure and buybacks, and resilience appears sufficient to avoid distress over twelve months, but not to hold cash interest cover at the current 3.23x if reported EBITDA falls sharply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Wayfair presents an adequate business profile supported by large scale, liquidity of USD 1,456 million (pro forma for the USD 64 million settlement of 2026-10-28: not established) and a laddered maturity profile, but credit quality is constrained by thin reported earnings, a working-capital float that depends on order volume, a growing block of secured debt and founder control with a large repurchase authority. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but not yet proven because free cash flow includes a working-capital inflow. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding earnings and on the 2027 convertible notes of USD 229 million being settled from cash. The primary downside path is an order decline that reverses the working-capital float while cash interest of USD 170 million stays fixed. Further analysis would require the debt documents, the proxy statement and a management outlook. Top Risk: working-capital reversal in an order decline.
